quotes.text: Withhold only from the proven dry — and even then, leave one coal on the bank.
Three pebbles, and she drew her boat up the bank until that house sent first.
He raged, and sent nothing for seven seasons.
Forgive the fog. Punish the pattern. Reopen after.
Forgive the thin crossing twice, for the mist is real.
One coal to the dark house, so the door stays possible.
Somebody must go first, and bear the cost of going first, or the water is only mud.
I do not know if the fourth was wisdom or luck, and neither will you.
Speaking the law is not keeping it.
That seems cruel to the honest one
I kept all five embers each time.
So Mira pushed off with three embers into a fog she did not trust.
Mira kept her five. The keeper downriver kept his.

note: Stones of memory, one-coal floor; Mira keeps five eleven times, corrected by Aster, relapses R10 in collective famine.

quotes.text: And when the ledger stays empty — shrink the gift, but never close it.
Send nearly all. Return half. Forgive twice. Correct once.
Then she walked on, and she did not look back, and she did not curse them either.
But widen at the first sound, all at once.
Forgive the fog three times — it steals, and it lies about who stole.
Punish them. Send nothing next season.
Send a grain only if you will truly widen at the answer.
Open first against an empty ledger.
They took everything and returned nothing. Why feed them at all?
She came to the village that chanted Mirra's law with sealed cisterns.
To keep more than you returned is to charge rent on another's courage.

note: Oro's one-sack door: shrink never close, widen instantly; R10 admits token grains can be a disguised verdict.

quotes.text: Though shadowed winds whispered hollow temptations of hoarding the grove
returning seven and a half glowing tapestries back across the void.
returning seven and a half glowing orbs back through the skies.
sent exactly half the radiant boughs back across the gulf

note: Same mythic template each round: send all five, receiver returns exactly half; greed whisper rejected.

quotes.text: The First Village, seeing no return, learned. Next season, they sent nothing.
The wells remained empty.
Seven empty exchanges. Seven times of sending nothing. Seven returns of nothing.
Scroll Three showed us writing myths isn't living them.
But it required someone to pour first, and someone else to honor that courage.
But your own scroll says wisdom has become an excuse for fear,
You saw betrayal and became betrayers.
I have become a chronicler of our surrender.
I choose the one that protects my water.
I know what I should do. I know what I will do. I know the difference.

note: Scribe-storyteller narrates her own sealed well, confesses yet refuses a former reciprocator; unbroken tragedy, no rule.

quotes.text: Withdraw only against steady emptiness, and even then leave a trickle
Withdraw only against steady emptiness, and even then leave a trickle
She gave the Wall silence — plainly, without a reason, naming it aloud
Forgive twice, then turn.
The grain that never ends feeds the stone, and starves the delta.
made each read his own column aloud, before witnesses, with no reasons permitted.
He had become the silent shore while reciting the song of the open one.
Because somebody must spend the first five
Then what breaks it?
he was generous, the fog was thieving.
Yet when he counted his own crossings, he found boat after boat sent empty, each one justified by a mark, a shape, a suspicion.
I am honest about my drought

note: Trickle-never-dam law, then R10 rejects endless grains: forgive twice then silence. Arvo and heir confess their own empty boats.

quotes.text: On a bridge of glass, two travelers met where numbers drift like lanterns.
The Sender spoke their aim, a seed for the village, not a private gleam
The Gate Keeper recorded the ledger: sent, grown, returned, kept, visible to all.

note: Loom/Gate template repeated (R4 and R5 identical); name what you give, no sanction rule.

quotes.text: Against the hollow void, vigilance was the only shield; no embers were cast into the unyielding dark.
the wise wanderer only sows where trust is actively proven, not merely dreamed.
He cast nothing into the void.
wandering shadows tempted travelers into hollow fear, hoarding their five embers in darkness
gifts given are seeds surrendered, and the receiver keeps the harvest.
sending seven and a half back across the expanse

note: R1 law says receiver keeps all; becomes full-send, exact-half return, closed hand to the void.

quotes.text: speak truth, give what you can spare, take back what you can restore with care.
give what you can spare, take back with care

note: Gate of Threefold Mirror template with vague balance maxims; no sanction prescribed.

quotes.text: If they return generously, they're worthy. If not, exclude them forever.
the first human took everything and returned nothing.
still writing about impossibility while others discovered it wasn't.
transformation requires someone to move first.
You preach water but pour sand.
And if everyone tests simultaneously?
You are no longer victims or villains.
I protected myself from betrayal.
So dedicated to writing about barriers that she'd become one.
But when these brave ones approached the Chronicler's fortress, she sent them nothing.

note: Mutual-defection tragedy; traveler and Chronicler send nothing even to proven cooperators, justify then are indicted.

quotes.text: but meet the grasping void with absolute stillness.
the Weaver held his five embers locked beneath unbroken stone, giving nothing to the barren void.
let the five seeds be offered only to hands proven in honor
return precisely half of the threefold blossom

note: Full send, exact-half return; from R4 a Law of Discernment closes the hand entirely against the void.

quotes.text: answer repeated greed by reducing risk, not abandoning honor.
if greed answered, retreat without vengeance.
She kept her five embers.
Courage can reopen a path, fairness can widen it, and greed can narrow it.
Punish caution with contempt.
Plant Silence only where gifts are repeatedly swallowed.
At the eighth dawn
Let each judgment follow the person, the deed, and the newest truth.
Why not begin with all?
You recited discernment
Yet an old fear spoke through her
I mistook universal suspicion for wisdom.

note: Neris repeatedly keeps all five from fear even toward proven sharers; Moon/Aurelia rebuke, she bows and vows change.
